question: Does a document VLM earn a place in this pipeline, and in which role?

candidate.path: transformers trust_remote_code (element-level); NOT the full PaddleOCR-VL pipeline, which needs PaddlePaddle

resource_state.classification: CLEAR at launch (0 MiB used, 0% util, no compute apps)
resource_state.note: an earlier attempt was correctly aborted mid-run by the guard when a neighbouring project claimed the GPU; this run completed on a clear device
resource_state.postflight: 0 MiB, no compute apps - nothing leaked

scoring: identical to experiments/008 - recall over each case's must_contain strings, NFC-normalized

verdict.rationale: 68% mean recall against adaptive's 93%, at roughly 40x the compute. It strictly beats every cheaper strategy on 1 of 10 cases (merged_cells, 100% vs 67%) and loses on 5, including 0% on stamp_over_text where the native text layer gives 100%.
verdict.en_vi_concern: 50% on clean_vi - a perfectly clean born-digital Vietnamese page - losing 'Hạnh phúc' and 'Nguyễn Thị Hương'. Vietnamese is half the production target, so this alone disqualifies it as a default for this population.
verdict.operational_complexity: its transformers path calls create_causal_mask(inputs_embeds=), a keyword absent from 4.53.3, 4.55.0, 4.57.6 and 5.16.1 - including the 4.55.0 its own config declares. A shim was required. It also needs a separate venv because paddleocr downgrades numpy/pyyaml in the validated environment.

limitations: element-level transformers path only; the full PaddleOCR-VL pipeline (with PP-DocLayoutV2 layout) was not evaluated and may score materially better as a page parser
no quantization or batching tried; latency is single-image, greedy, max_new_tokens=1024
